Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are PineStreet's redlines to the MSA and Order Form focused on IP ownership and use of outputs. High-level asks:

- Customer retains exclusive ownership of outputs (including text, code, and derived artifacts) generated using Customer prompts/datasets.
- No model retraining or incorporation of Customer data for model updates without explicit written consent from PineStreet.

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding PineStreet's redlines. Key asks on ownership and training opt-out. Can you review and propose narrow language we can push back with?

My read: they want a full output assignment + no training ever. I think we can accept customer ownership of outputs used in their product, but we need the following limited carveouts:

- A telemetry/feedback license scoped to aggregated, de-identified data used solely for product quality and safety improvements (no model retraining for customer-specific data unless paid and explicitly agreed).
- A narrow operational exception to use minimal logs for emergency debugging and security patching (time-limited retention, audit trail).
- A commercial surcharge for opting out of our general improvement pool (covers lost signal).

Please annotate the attached redlines with suggested text and turnaround by EOD tomorrow if possible — they are asking to close this week. Attachment: PSL_MSA_Redlines_20261129.docx

Jonas / Marissa — I reviewed their doc and drafted compromise language below. High-level approach: grant Customer ownership of outputs but preserve a tightly scoped "Feedback & Operational Data License" for Redwood. Proposed snippets below can be pasted into the MSA and Order Form.

1) Output Rights (Order Form / Use Rights)
"Customer shall own all right, title and interest in and to Outputs created solely from Customer Input and Customer Content. For the avoidance of doubt, Outputs do not include: (i) aggregated, de-identified metrics and telemetry that do not identify Customer or Customer Users; or (ii) Redwood's pre-existing models, model weights, or any model artifacts that are not derived from Customer Content."

2) Feedback & Operational Data License (MSA Section X)
"Customer hereby grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Feedback and Operational Data solely to operate, troubleshoot, and improve Redwood's services in aggregated and de-identified form. 'Feedback and Operational Data' excludes any Customer Content and excludes Outputs to the extent Customer has marked Outputs as confidential in accordance with Section Y. Redwood shall not use Feedback and Operational Data to retrain or update model weights in a manner that results in Customer-identifiable data being incorporated into models without Customer's prior written consent."

3) Emergency Debugging / Security Exception
"Notwithstanding the above, Redwood may access unredacted logs or Outputs where necessary to respond to a security incident or material service degradation. Redwood will: (i) limit access to named engineers; (ii) notify Customer within 48 hours after access where feasible; and (iii) retain such data only for a period necessary to remediate the issue, not to exceed 90 days unless required by applicable law or pursuant to audit requests agreed by both parties."

4) Commercial for Training Opt-Out
"Where Customer elects to affirmatively opt-out of any use of Customer Content or Outputs for model training, Redwood may apply a commercial surcharge to the Order Form to offset increased costs and lost signal. Surcharge details (if any) will be set forth in the Order Form."

I can convert the above into redline text for the docx and send a clean suggested language file. Also recommend we propose a 12-month audit window for aggregated metrics and an SLA for response to security access requests.

-Kimberly Park

Liz — thanks for sending the redlines and for the call. Kimberly's suggested language (copied below) is our proposed middle ground. In short:

- PineStreet keeps ownership of Outputs generated from your inputs;
- Redwood keeps the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product safety and improvement, but we will not incorporate Customer-identifiable data into model weights without explicit, paid consent;
- We will include an emergency-access carveout for security/bug fixes with strict access controls and a 90-day retention cap.

Proposed next step: if PineStreet is comfortable in principle, Kimberly will produce a tracked-change redline and we can circulate. Also note that electing a training opt-out will require a small commercial surcharge; we can surface numbers in the Order Form addendum. I have attached a plain-text version of the proposed snippets for legal review.

Attachment: Redwood_Suggested_Language_20261129.txt

Would you be able to confirm principle agreement on the three bullets above so we can progress to redlines and DocuSign this week?

Jonas / Kimberly — appreciate the quick turnaround and the thoughtful language. PineStreet is generally aligned with the three bullets as an initial commercial compromise, subject to:

- A precise definition of "de-identified" and technical measures to ensure irreversibility (we'll expect an annex describing hashing/aggregation thresholds);
- An explicit carveout that allows Redwood to access unredacted logs for security and safety but only under a documented request process and with an audit trail;
- Confirmation that the surcharge for training opt-out is a one-time fee (preferable) or a clear formula if recurring.

If you can send the tracked redline and the annex on anonymization thresholds, we can get our procurement and security teams to sign off. We're keen to close this month.
